rationale: Both texts narrate the same baptism, checkable directly by reading the two side by side: the divine voice's Greek wording matches exactly except at one point, checked directly against both texts for this lesson -- Matthew's third-person Houtos estin ("This is") against Mark's second-person Sy ei ("You are"), with the rest of the clause (ho huios mou ho agapetos, en [-] eudokesa) identical. Matthew's own account of John's objection and Jesus's answer about fulfilling all righteousness (3:14-15) has no counterpart anywhere in Mark's account, which moves directly from Jesus's arrival (1:9) to His baptism (1:9) to the Spirit's descent (1:10) with no recorded exchange between John and Jesus. The label is strong rather than explicit because neither Gospel names or cites the other as its source for this scene.
